rows.requirement: Absolute drive paths, drive case, Unicode and spaces retain their intended syntax.
Baseline relative and network path forms convert without filesystem traversal.
Drive-relative, bare drive, current drive roots, absolute resolution and per-drive cwd are observed explicitly.
Dot traversal, root boundaries, trailing delimiters and repeated/mixed separators cover all path classes.
Ordinary drive roots and Windows drive-relative rendering are checked with and without absolute conversion.
UNC fallback preserves source syntax where official runtime does; share roots, traversal, repeated separators and POSIX UNC are represented.
Already requested syntax is accepted for POSIX, Windows and mixed input, including relative dots.
Filename escaping, reserved spelling, trailing dot/space and drive-like colon forms are separately exercised.
Measured root, nested mount, component boundaries and proc mapping precedence control conversion.
Root reverse mapping and case-sensitive mount boundaries are checked.
Stable proc drive prefix remains available independently of native prefix.
All output type names and explicit UTF-8 selectors are represented.
Short root-local applies to ordinary absolute drive/UNC output; list and long option behaviors are observed separately.
Ordinary extended drive and UNC namespaces are checked for each output type and root-local combination.
GNU permutation, combined/repeated flags, attached arguments, case aliases, ignored modifiers and dash operands are independently represented.
Windows list delimiter and empty list policy are observed.
Interior and boundary empty list members cover both source syntaxes.
List idempotence, mixed/absolute/proc output and non-ASCII spaces are covered.
The ordinary stdin record protocol matches argv conversion.
Empty streams/records, BOM position, final record, CRLF and spaces are explicit.
BOM-only, terminal CR, NUL, spaces, empty record ignore and fgets-size boundaries retain native input semantics.
Immutable byte files exercise LF/CRLF/final record, BOM, empty input/record, partial failure and per-record options.
Option lines reset getopt state, preserve path spaces and subsequent ordinary-record state.
A later invalid operand preserves earlier output; ignore behavior and literal record delimiters are tested.
Ignored empty operands do not terminate conversion of valid later operands.
Invalid combinations, type, unknown option, missing option argument/operand and per-line parse failures are retained exact comparisons.
Historical invalid UTF-8 bytes remain raw observations; only strict project rejection is a defined contract.
Malformed first/second records, prefixes/suffixes, truncated sequences, long preceding allocation and Windows output are rejected deterministically by the project.
